tracker: the review, the closed item, and the merge (refs WI-0003)

WI-0003 merged into main and closed as delivered, and EP-001 closed behind it as its last
child. This commit carries the epic's closure: DE1-DE6 walked criterion by criterion, with
DE3 answered by running the merged tool rather than by reading what the items claimed.

All seven success measures met. Persistence across seven separate processes; the worked
example giving exactly Bob pays Alice 10.00 and Carol pays Alice 10.00; the amounts netting
to zero by construction and over ten stores; nineteen bad invocations across all five
commands, every one exiting 2 with a message and no traceback; no non-stdlib import, no
packaging file, and every module parsing under Python 3.9; settling up in one command; and
the net positions alongside that let somebody check the answer instead of trusting it.

DE6 found one false sentence and corrected it rather than carrying it. The overview claimed
the tool reads no environment beyond EXPENSES_STORE; store_path() also reads XDG_DATA_HOME,
exactly as ADR-0002 decision 1 specifies -- the code and the ADR were right and only the
document's summary of them was wrong. Overview to v5. No item's own D12 would have caught
it, which is what DE6 is for. DE4 added "What is actually built" to the vision at v4, so a
reader arriving after closure can tell delivery from intent without opening the tracker.

Two limitations outlive the epic and are recorded on it: a hand-edited store can hold a
negative amount that reaches the settlement arithmetic and yields a report that adds up and
means nothing; and nothing static-analyses this code, because ADR-0001 takes no dependency
and the standard library ships no linter, so lint-clean was skipped -- never passed -- on
all three items.

Deferred work is scoped, not forgotten: recording a repayment has a seam built for it and
asserted on settle.py's import graph, and the bank-CSV import waits only on a sample export.

longside, computed as two separate stages so a repayment can later net in as one more transfer.

Two things worth your attention:

- **DE6 earned its place.** The architecture overview claimed the tool reads no environment variable beyond `EXPENSES_STORE`; `store.store_path()` also reads `XDG_DATA_HOME`, exactly as ADR-0002 specifies. The code and the ADR were right and only the document's summary was wrong — and no item's own D12 would have caught it, because no item touched that function. Corrected at overview v5.
- **Nothing static-analyses this code**, on any item. `commands.lint` is `null` because ADR-0001 takes no dependency and the standard library ships no linter, so the gate was recorded as *skipped* three times running. It has cost something real each time — this item nearly shipped an unused parameter, and the review found a comment naming a module that does not exist. Recorded on EP-001 as a standing limitation.

Toolkit friction is in `HARNESS-STATUS.md`; the sharpest is that the `history.md` and `board.md` write-guards match on the command *text*, so they blocked a journal append that merely mentioned `history.md` in prose, and blocked `cat tracker/board.md` outright.
